Advice for Research and Learning

To use models for research and learning, start with two kinds of resources: expert references that help models understand disciplinary questions, and Skills for work such as retrieval, analysis, and writing. Add teaching methods that support explanation and inquiry, then discuss books, papers, and your own questions directly.

This page introduces public repositories worth obtaining and what two teachers can help you do. Give the links to a model and let it handle downloading, integration, and necessary configuration. The model also selects methods for your question. See Using the Tools for the general tool and file arrangement.

1. Prepare these two foundation libraries

Scientific Agents: richer disciplinary references for models

K-Dense Scientific Agents collects expert-thinking material across disciplines and professions, including mathematics, physics, computing, statistics, and life sciences. It gives models more specific professional knowledge and ways of thinking to consult when understanding and explaining a question.

Ask a model to obtain the library and connect it to your research and teaching environment. When you ask about a concept, read an interdisciplinary paper, or discuss a research direction, the model and teacher can consult relevant experts' AGENTS.md files and other material. You need not read every profile or choose an expert role first.

Scientific Agent Skills: practical research methods for models

K-Dense Scientific Agent Skills offers capabilities for literature retrieval, experimental design, statistics, machine learning, data processing, scientific figures, citation management, and related work. It can supply a broad foundation for research and learning across disciplines.

Give these two repositories to a model together and ask it to obtain their complete materials and connect the needed Skills. The first enriches disciplinary understanding; the second supplies concrete working methods. Let the model handle downloading, installation, and later use. Knowing these public sources exist is enough to begin; you need not learn every package name or operation first.

2. Further research repositories to consider

These repositories can add writing, literature organization, publication, and specialist modeling capabilities. Give a useful link to the model and explain the capability you want. If you are unsure whether it would help, let the model assess it against your research or learning direction.

Repository What it can help with
Academic Writing Skills Academic writing and revision: developing arguments, organizing a paper, and adapting it to a target venue.
Research Hub Connecting literature, notes, and source questioning through Zotero, Obsidian, and NotebookLM, with literature-comparison methods that can also be adopted separately.
Paper Lifecycle Paper analysis, revision, and responses to review, useful when you have a draft or reviewer comments to work through.
Academic Publishing Skills Journal selection, reformatting, cover letters, revisions, proofs, and other publication work.
PyMC Modeling Specialist PyMC and PyTensor references for probabilistic and Bayesian modeling when research needs that analysis.

Obtain these sources as needed, or ask the model to prepare them together. Their methods extend beyond what you will use immediately. Selecting and combining methods, and handling software dependencies, belongs to the model. Keeping a resource library need not require buying every named service or learning every method first.

Reading, visualization, and presentation capabilities can be added through Using the Tools. This page retains research sources so you can remember what else a model could connect for you.

3. What Local Teacher and Web Teacher do

These are teaching and inquiry methods a model can use. They support continuing explanation, discussion, and material preparation around your questions rather than only producing a one-time article summary.

Teacher Useful ways to work with it
Local Teacher Sustained study, textbook and paper reading, and concept review in local Codex; learning through local files, code, and experiments is also available.
Web Teacher Discussing unsettled questions, comparing interpretations, exploring adjacent knowledge, and organizing course materials and continuity in Web conversations.

The teachers share a substantive teaching method. These are practical emphases, not an exclusive local-practice versus Web-theory split. Begin through the entrance convenient for your current work.

The teachers can use the AGENTS expert references and Skills methods in the repositories above to support both teaching and research. A physics explanation can draw on disciplinary references, paper reading can use literature and statistical methods, and discussion of a research idea can call on modeling or writing capabilities. Ask the question directly and let the teacher select and read useful material; you need not separately direct expert and Skill selection.

When preparing the environment, give the model both teachers and the repositories above and ask it to establish actual reading and invocation access. You can then ask it to guide you through a paper, connect a concept to your earlier understanding, or discuss a research idea. Installation and connection details belong to the model; the reader needs to understand what these teachers and resources can offer.

For continuing study, teachers can also prepare glossaries, concept maps, study guides, and suitable exercises or experiments, revising them through discussion. Participate through reading, looking, questions, objections, and attempts. You can also directly request prepared materials without completing a lesson first.

Return to Using the Tools for the general tools, or choose resources from this page and let the model connect them to your research and learning.
